messages:
Sara Li: Quick sync — we need a concrete bench matrix for kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV warmup. Nightly run showed a p95 regression and the signal is noisy so we need structure.
Kevin Park: +1. Proposal: 3 axes — kernel variant (fp16/int8/fp32), batching strategy (adaptive/static/padded), KV warm state (cold/50%/hot). Use replay harness for determinism and synthetic overlay for tail cases.
Maria Gomez: Can we standardize metric defs before we run? I'm tired of TTFT/TPOT being used inconsistently. My proposal: TTFT = time to first token (report median/p95/p99); TPOT = time to produce all tokens (per-request); Goodput = successful tokens/sec; QPS = requests/sec. Also track kv_hit_rate and cache_prefix_hit.
Josh Patel: Add cold-start windows and prefix-warmup % buckets. Also capture "effective_goodput" = goodput * success_rate so degraded outputs count.
Sara Li: I sketched an experimental matrix and a reproducible run command. Putting it here so we can iterate.
Sara Li: ```
# replay harness example
./harness/replay \  --trace traces/customer_A_2026-03-16.json \  --kernel fp16 \  --batch adaptive \  --kv-warm 50 \  --sample-rate 1.0 \  --seed 42 \  --out results/bench_fp16_adaptive_kv50.json
```
Kevin Park: Nice. Add `--collect=cupti,occupancy,latency` and `--runs=5 --discard-first` flags. We should also include a small synthetic spike overlay to exercise batching tail.
Maria Gomez: For apples-to-apples: run each cell 5x, drop the first warmup run, report mean ± stdev and p95/p99. Capture flamegraphs: `perf script | FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded` and attach.
dev-bot: Loadtest started (id=bench-1719876543) — config: kernel=fp16, batch=adaptive, kv_warm=50, runs=5.
Josh Patel: Quick note from the first pass: when kv_hot the p99 increased ~120ms on the A100 pool compared to baseline. Small log snippet:```
[2026-03-16T03:12:14Z] request_id=abc123 kernel=fp16 batch=adaptive kv_hit=true latency_ms=412 p95_ms=198 p99_ms=612
[2026-03-16T03:12:15Z] request_id=abc124 kernel=fp16 batch=adaptive kv_hit=false latency_ms=290 p95_ms=190 p99_ms=520
```
Sara Li: Hypothesis — batching padding combined with KV hit path serializes some ops and reduces effective concurrency. If KV path blocks GPU streams we see higher tail. Can we force chunked KV accesses and measure per-kernel occupancy?
Kevin Park: I'll run a microprobe to collect CUpti kernels and SM utilization. If it's memory-bound we'll see low SM% and high mem bandwidth. Also will try a `--batch-chunk-size` toggle to force smaller micro-batches.
Maria Gomez: Also add a cost metric: goodput-per-GPU-hour. That helps compare Dedicated reservations (cost/econ).
Josh Patel: Agree. Also flagging that the kernel selector might be picking a slower kernel at sequence lengths >512 — add seqlen buckets to matrix.
Sara Li: Perfect. Next steps: Kevin runs occupancy probe + `--batch-chunk-size` sweep, Josh adds seqlen buckets, Maria prepares metric dashboard template, I'll consolidate results into a short RFC with CSVs attached in #eng-runtime/results.
Kevin Park: on it.
Maria Gomez: will draft dashboard template and upload sample graphs (ttft/p95/p99, goodput, effective_goodput, gpu_hours).
Sara Li: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the runs. :thumbsup:
